reader.requirement: At --std 85 the word SYNC must be accepted wherever SYNCHRONIZED is, in both forms of the format (with or without LEFT/RIGHT), and must mean the same clause, held to the same rules: allowed on an elementary item, refused on a group (SR1), refused on an index item (§1985:VI.5.14.3 SR6), and counted as the same clause when duplicated. The witness covers only the group-refusal half.

edition-consulted.switches: word status of SYNC / SYNCHRONIZED (both rows reserved at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023 in ReservedWords.Table.cs#Entries)
DialectLevel >= 2023 lets a group carry the clause; below that it is refused with COBOL0900 (Constructs.SyncOnGroup2023). The 85 arm differs from the latest one and matches §1985:VI.5.13.3 SR1
dialectLevel < 2002 refuses SYNCHRONIZED on a usage-INDEX item (§1985:VI.5.14.3 SR6). The 85 arm differs from the latest one and is correct

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the abbreviation itself: one token alternative (SYNCHRONIZED | SYNC) feeds one bound flag at every edition. The clause's placement rules differ: group items are refused below 2023 and index items below 2002, and both spellings take the same arm.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness checks only that SYNC on a group is refused below 2023. The accepted elementary forms (SYNC, SYNC LEFT, SYNC RIGHT), the index refusal and the duplicate-clause identity are not exercised.

probes.expected: SYNC / SYNCHRONIZED, each with no phrase, LEFT and RIGHT, on signed and unsigned COMP and on alphanumeric items, compile and behave identically

probes.printed: COBOL0900 on G1 (SYNCHRONIZED) and on G2 (SYNC): SYNCHRONIZED on a group item requires COBOL-2023
probes.expected: both spellings refused on a group (§1985:VI.5.13.3 SR1)

probes.printed: COBOL2405 on I1 (SYNC) and on I2 (SYNCHRONIZED), citing §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR6
probes.expected: both spellings refused on a usage-INDEX item at 85 (the 1985-only exclusion)

probes.printed: COBOL2423: the clause 'SYNC' is written 2 times (for PIC 9(4) COMP SYNC SYNCHRONIZED)
probes.expected: SYNC and SYNCHRONIZED are one clause, so writing both is a duplicate

OK  §1985:VI.5.13.3 SR1  (5.13.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: The lexer has two tokens, and syncClause takes either one. BindEntry reads only the LEFT/RIGHT phrase, so nothing after the parser can tell the spellings apart. Every placement rule probed (group, index, duplicate) treats SYNC and SYNCHRONIZED identically at 85.

refuter.evidence: rsy1 (run, --std 85): 77 S9(4) COMP SYNC VALUE -7, SYNC LEFT / SYNCHRONIZED RIGHT inside OCCURS 3, SYNC on a REDEFINES of PIC X(4), SYNC on PACKED-DECIMAL after a PIC X; printed '-0007 +23456 -00022 +00333 / 004 055 666 B / 1234 -987654321' (MOVE 123456 to S9(5) COMP SYNC truncates to 23456: the original PICTURE size governs, §1985:VI.5.13.4 GR5). rsy2: SYNC on a 66 RENAMES -> COBOL0001 syntax error (correct: format 2 has no SYNC). rsy3: SYNC on 88 -> COBOL1747; SYNC RIGHT on 01 group -> COBOL0900 (SR1); SYNC and SYNCHRONIZED LEFT on elementary items INHERITING group USAGE INDEX -> COBOL2405 citing §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR6 (the inherited half the reader did not probe). Both spellings behave identically everywhere. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.13.3 SR2; OK §1985:VI.5.13.3 SR1; OK §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR6; OK §1985:VI.5.13.4 GR5.
